text.en: The Holy Family Hymns of 1860, where James Chadwick's English began, marks the verse "Solo" and the Gloria "Chorus". Its preface explains: a few singers who know the tune sing the verse, and the whole congregation answers.
text.es: The Holy Family Hymns, de 1860, donde empezó la versión inglesa de James Chadwick, marca la estrofa como "Solo" y el Gloria como "Chorus" (coro). Su prefacio lo explica: unos pocos cantantes que conocen la melodía cantan la estrofa, y toda la congregación responde.

source.en: The Holy Family Hymns, with Music for the Holy Family Hymns (London: Richardson and Son, 1860), preface, p. viii, and music, pp. 8 and 9, read from the scan
source.es: The Holy Family Hymns, with Music for the Holy Family Hymns (Londres: Richardson and Son, 1860), prefacio, p. viii, y música, pp. 8 y 9, leído en el escaneo

text.en: In the Latin Bible, Luke's angels sing "Gloria in altissimis Deo". The carol's "in excelsis" comes from the Gloria of the Mass, the ancient hymn that opens with the angels' song in those words.
text.es: En la Biblia latina, los ángeles de Lucas cantan "Gloria in altissimis Deo". El "in excelsis" del villancico viene del Gloria de la misa, el antiguo himno que empieza con el canto de los ángeles en esas palabras.

source.en: Latin Vulgate, Luke 2:14, at DRBO.org; Adrian Fortescue, "Gloria in Excelsis Deo", The Catholic Encyclopedia, vol. 6 (New York: Robert Appleton Company, 1909)
source.es: Vulgata latina, Lucas 2:14, en DRBO.org; Adrian Fortescue, "Gloria in Excelsis Deo", The Catholic Encyclopedia, vol. 6 (Nueva York: Robert Appleton Company, 1909)
